posts.content_md:
Joe, I have been accused of whining, foot stomping etc... because I post something and no one responds and repost asking for some type of feedback. I have also been accused of chest thumping if I try to present what I think a novel application or idea concerning holography. I have since learned I will post anyway.

It does seem there are a lot of members that do take in all the information without contributing. This is very evident if you look at this past December. There were 92 users on line on that single day. Sometimes I see 10-15-20 or more users on line at one time but only a small handful of members post anything at all or even comment on a post. How many people have contributed to the Wiki?

I am not sure why more persons do not post more??? It may be that a certain someone in the past used to belittle me if I brought up "ideas" or asked a question that was supposed to be known or seem too simple. Maybe it’s that we have so much information on the Wiki and in prior forum posts that most questions are already answered. Maybe the new subject are over the heads of most members so they don’t want to take a chance on being make a fool or being wrong so they just keep quiet.

This is also evident in the fact that the attendance at the PCGIII was 0 after I decided not to drive 10 hours with no one else attending. I feel for John K. as I am sure he went through great lengths in acquiring the inexpensive housing units, preparing for cave holography, setting up his hex table, preparing his house in addition to me boxing all my stuff up I was going to take and then had to unbox it all. I was really disappointed.

I understand there are probably some professionals here that lurk only so that they may get an idea, concept or technique that they can adapt to make them money without compensation to the poster but it has to be that the majority of members are amateurs, as I am, and why they do not post I do not know. 

Joe, do not feel the least bit bad about not sharing information you do not want to. I know for a fact that the two banned users check this forum often. In fact one has the audacity to e-mail me with a personal attack concerning a post I made on this forum. I think your approach of sharing a good find with only those that you know and that ask is a good one and is rightfully respected. You do share and you do contribute and for that I am grateful. Maybe if the majority of members that contribute here did the same, that is discuss a idea and it's potential but never disclose the solution publicly but only privately to known posters, then more would be inclined to participate to be within the known. As much as I hate that idea, it may work. It's really sad that it seems most holographers still need to work alone and keep quiet.

I was/am an idealist and I thought for sure this is the age of the internet and that holographers will finally get together and share all their ideas so that more holographer can come up with new ideas and not have to re-invent the wheel and will bring better and newer products to the marketplace thus opening the eyes of the public that their is a place for holography. But it still may not be time, it may never be, I don't know. Maybe it is the time and the pro’s are doing it at our expense.

Ok, sorry, I had to get that off my chest.

Peace! 

Oh, and thank you!

posts.content_md:
Although the member list had seemed to approach 500 or so, I wonder how many of them have labs and do anything holographic?

The number of people who really pursue holography in the hopes of making some sort of display has to number only in the dozens in the US by my estimation. Here in Chicago, for instance, as far as I know in regards to actual shooting holographers, there is myself, Rick Bruck, TJ at LFC, the lab at the School of the Art Institute and that's about it. Of course there are the looney tunes that run the so-called Museum of Holography, but they have done more than their share to discourage people from entering the medium. I could name at least 100 people over the years who have talked about setting up labs but have never even bought a laser!

I really cherish this Forum, because it renews my hope that this medium will go somewhere. Here are the amateurs in the truest sense of the word, with the Latin root *amo*, love, who are doing this because they are in love with the medium. And there is an insane commitment of time (forget about the money) that this love affair demands!

I can see the frustration with posting stuff and no comment or reply, I know with my lifestyle I don't often get the chance, except for today when it seems like I have diahrrea of the keyboard! All this writing has taken about an hour! 

But it has always been a dedicated very few that are doing what we are doing! When I put together my list of Top Ten Art Holographers, I have to add myself to the list to come up with 10!

posts.topic_title: To post or not to post...
posts.author: Joe Farina
posts.post_subject: To post or not to post...
posts.content_md:
To be honest, I'm beginning to take offense at the tone of some of the postings on this thread. Really I'm too busy to spend time on this, but since some of the responses are so lengthy, I feel like my position is being overpowered by the sheer weight of those words. Please, don't anyone object by saying "we said it's a personal decision, so don't be offended." The tone is clear, so save your breath.

I almost always share what I know on this forum. In fact, I share practically everything, if I think it's relevant to the discussion. But there have been two instances where I've worked very hard to achieve something, and I don't wish to share these particular things with everyone on the planet. I don't *like* everyone on the planet. The first thing was a new sealing method/material for DCG. The second was the water-cooled/heated coating plate.

Regarding the first, that's a true secret that I've kept to myself. So no one needs to bother asking about it. Regarding the second, I've already made full disclosures to three people on this forum, and I figure that if anyone is really interested, they can send me a personal message, and I can decide whether or not I want to reply. As a matter of fact, the three people I disclosed it to have participated in this thread, and two of them have made it clear that their own, personal position is a more "honorable" one: they will disclose everything they know, for the greater glory of holography. What a pain.

posts.content_md:
Hi all

I have to confess to being one of the 'lurkers'. I am based in the UK and I am VERY new to holography. Six months ago I basically didn't know holography even existed as an amateur hobby.

It all started when I was browsing Ebay one evening with a glass of Southern Comfort in hand. I came across someone selling a HeNe laser - The hour was late, the alcohol had eased my pain and I ended up placing a bid for that laser. I can't even begin to think why I even placed a bid, but I ended up winning the auction.

Suffice to say that's the last time I browse Ebay with the SC anywhere near !! Anyway, the laser arrived, I plugged it in and marvelled at the tiny red dot (sad I know!). This fascination lasted about 10 minutes before I had started to hunt for something else to do with my 'new toy'.

I turned to Google and started to search... And Holography came up! I thought to myself 'now there's an interesting subject and so I started to look up as many holography related sites as I could find including this one. I joined as a member and introduced myself.

Thanks to this forum I have learned loads of information in quite a short space of time. I am now well and truly hooked on what I see as wonderful new hobby. So far i've only produced some simple Denisyuk holograms, but the feeling of pride seeing that first faint image with black parallel lines running through it will never leave me.

Since then i've been getting more and more successful with each attempt, my holograms are getting brighter, the parallel lines are gone, my squegeeing is improving and i've learned how to use TEA.

I have to confess to having had the help and advice (by email) of a professional holographer here in the UK. But and it's a big BUT, without this forum and the wiki I wouldn't have been able to learn anywhere near as much as I have in the short time i've been involved.

I read the forum most days and marvel at the knowledge that some of you people have, I read and learn in the hope that one day I may be able to make a useful contribution to the group without making a fool of myself. I try not to ask too many questions until I have searched for the answers myself, that way i'm not seen as someone who is always taking and never giving anything back.

I can honestly say that were it not for this forum my interest in holography would not have been stimulated in the way it has. SO, a BIG thank you to you all for all your help and advice, even if you didn't know you were giving it.

Cheers

Jem
